title: Joshua Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 13.

questions.question: In Joshua 13, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Joshua was old and stricken in years
The land of the Giblites and all Lebanon
Divide the land for an inheritance unto the nine tribes
The land that remaineth: all the borders of the Philistines and all Geshuri
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua was old and stricken in years
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:1 states first that Joshua was old and stricken in years, which is the earliest event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: According to Joshua 13, who spoke to Joshua about the remaining land to be possessed?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:1 states that the LORD said unto Joshua about the land that remaineth to be possessed.

questions.question: Which peoples' borders are mentioned as part of the land that remaineth to be possessed?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:2 explicitly states the land that remaineth includes all the borders of the Philistines, and all Geshuri.

questions.question: From where to where does the text describe the land of the five lords of the Philistines?
options: From Sihor before Egypt to the borders of Ekron northward
From the Jordan River to the Dead Sea
From Aphek to the borders of the Amorites
questions.correctAnswer: From Sihor before Egypt to the borders of Ekron northward
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:3 describes the land of the five lords of the Philistines from Sihor before Egypt to the borders of Ekron northward.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as one of the five lords of the Philistines in Joshua 13?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:3 lists the Gazathites, Ashdothites, Eshkalonites, Gittites, and Ekronites as the five lords of the Philistines; Moabites are not listed.

questions.question: According to Joshua 13, to what borders does the land of the Canaanites and Mearah extend?
options: From the north to the borders of Geshur
From the south to Aphek, to the borders of the Amorites
From Lebanon to the entering into Hamath
From Aroer to the city in the river Arnon
questions.correctAnswer: From the south to Aphek, to the borders of the Amorites
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:4 describes the land from the south, all the land of the Canaanites and Mearah beside the Sidonians, unto Aphek, to the borders of the Amorites.

questions.question: Which land is described as extending from Baalgad under Mount Hermon to Hamath?
options: The land of the Giblites and all Lebanon
questions.correctAnswer: The land of the Giblites and all Lebanon
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:5 states the land of the Giblites and all Lebanon extends toward the sunrising from Baalgad under Mount Hermon unto the entering into Hamath.

questions.question: Who does the LORD say He will drive out from before the children of Israel?
options: The inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon unto Misrephothmaim and all the Sidonians
questions.correctAnswer: The inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon unto Misrephothmaim and all the Sidonians
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:6 states the LORD will drive out all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon unto Misrephothmaim, and all the Sidonians before the children of Israel.

questions.question: What instruction is given to Joshua regarding the remaining land?
options: To conquer all the land immediately
To divide it by lot unto the Israelites for an inheritance
To leave it for future generations
To give it to the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: To divide it by lot unto the Israelites for an inheritance
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:6 commands Joshua to divide the land by lot unto the Israelites for an inheritance as the LORD commanded.

questions.question: To how many tribes and half tribes is Joshua instructed to divide the land?
options: Nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh
Seven tribes and the half tribe of Gad
questions.correctAnswer: Nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:7 instructs Joshua to divide the land for an inheritance unto the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh.

questions.question: Which tribes had already received their inheritance beyond Jordan eastward as given by Moses?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:8 states that the Reubenites and Gadites received their inheritance beyond Jordan eastward as Moses gave them.

questions.question: From where to where does the inheritance of the Reubenites and Gadites extend?
options: From Aroer upon the bank of the river Arnon to Dibon
From Mount Hermon to the sea
From the Jordan River to the Dead Sea
From Aphek to the borders of the Amorites
questions.correctAnswer: From Aroer upon the bank of the river Arnon to Dibon
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:9 specifies their land from Aroer, upon the bank of the river Arnon, and all the plain of Medeba unto Dibon.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 13 states that the LORD commanded Joshua to divide the land by lot for the Israelites.
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:6 clearly states that Joshua should divide the land by lot unto the Israelites as the LORD commanded.

questions.question: True or False: The land of the Geshurites and Maachathites is included in the inheritance described in Joshua 13.
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:11 includes Gilead and the borders of the Geshurites and Maachathites as part of the land to be possessed.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 13 mentions that the Philistines were given land as an inheritance.
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:6 states the inhabitants, including the Philistines, will be driven out, not given land as inheritance.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei?
questions.explanation: The verse states that all the kingdom of Og in Bashan reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei (Joshua 13:12).

questions.question: What does Joshua 13:14 promise will happen if someone follows the LORD's command regarding sacrifices?
options: They will receive land as an inheritance
They will be victorious in battle
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:14 indicates that the tribe of Levi was not given an inheritance because their inheritance was the sacrifices made to the LORD.

questions.question: Which tribe received inheritance according to their families?
questions.explanation: Moses gave unto the tribe of the children of Reuben inheritance according to their families (Joshua 13:15).

questions.question: What towns are mentioned in Joshua 13:17 as part of Heshbon and its cities?
questions.explanation: Heshbon and all her cities in the plain include Dibon, and Kirjathaim as stated in Joshua 13:17.

questions.question: What does Joshua 13:18 indicate about the cities listed?
options: They were located in the desert
questions.explanation: The cities mentioned, including Jahazah and Kedemoth, are noted as being part of the plain in Joshua 13:18.

questions.question: What was located in the mount of the valley according to Joshua 13:19?
questions.explanation: Zarethshahar is mentioned as being in the mount of the valley in Joshua 13:19.

questions.question: What kingdom did Moses smite along with its princes?
questions.explanation: The kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites was smote by Moses and is detailed in Joshua 13:21.

questions.question: What did the children of Israel do to Balaam according to Joshua 13:22?
questions.explanation: The children of Israel slayed Balaam the son of Beor with the sword among those who were slain (Joshua 13:22).

questions.question: How does Joshua 13:3 describe the borders of Ekron?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:3 states that the borders of Ekron are northward, counted to the Canaanite.

questions.question: What command is given to Joshua in Joshua 13:7?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:7 commands Joshua to divide the land for an inheritance unto the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh.

questions.question: What did God promise to do in Joshua 13:6 regarding the Sidonians?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:6 states that God will drive out the Sidonians from before the children of Israel.

questions.question: What was the inheritance of the tribe of Levi according to Joshua 13:14?
questions.explanation: The tribe of Levi was given the sacrifices made by fire as their inheritance (Joshua 13:14).

questions.question: True or False: The Geshurites and the Maachathites were expelled from Israel according to Joshua 13:13.
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:13 states that the children of Israel did not expel the Geshurites and Maachathites; they dwell among the Israelites.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua was young and strong when he received the command to divide the land according to Joshua 13:1.
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:1 indicates that Joshua was old and stricken in years when he received the command.

questions.question: True or False: The cities of the plain were included in the territory of Sihon king of the Amorites according to Joshua 13:21.
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:21 confirms that all the cities of the plain were part of the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 13.

questions.question: What river marked the border of the inheritance of the children of Reuben?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:23 states, 'And the border of the children of Reuben was Jordan, and the border thereof.'

questions.question: Who gave inheritance to the tribe of Gad according to Joshua 13?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:24 clearly says, 'And Moses gave inheritance unto the tribe of Gad, even unto the children of Gad according to their families.'

questions.question: Which city is mentioned as part of the coast of the children of Gad?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:25 states, 'And their coast was Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon.'

questions.question: What is the eastern border mentioned for the children of Gad's inheritance?
options: Edge of the sea of Chinnereth
questions.correctAnswer: Edge of the sea of Chinnereth
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:27 notes, 'Jordan and his border, even unto the edge of the sea of Chinnereth on the other side Jordan eastward.'

questions.question: Which tribe is mentioned as receiving no inheritance in the land?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:33 says, 'But unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave not any inheritance: the LORD God of Israel was their inheritance.'

questions.question: How many cities in Bashan were part of the inheritance of the half tribe of Manasseh?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:30 states, 'all the towns of Jair, which are in Bashan, threescore cities.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'nachalah' in Joshua 13:24 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'nachalah' (נַחֲלָה) in Joshua 13:24 means 'inheritance' or 'possession,' referring to the land allocated to tribes.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominent in Joshua 13:15-33 as the chapter systematically lists tribal inheritances?
questions.explanation: The passage forms an inclusio by starting and ending with Moses’ distribution of land and the special case of Levi's inheritance (Joshua 13:15 and 13:33) framing the entire section.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage similarly discusses land allocation to tribes, paralleling Joshua 13:7?
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:52-56 describes the land allotment to the tribes of Israel, which is directly connected to Joshua 13:7 where the land division is commanded.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the concept of God as inheritance, as seen with the tribe of Levi in Joshua 13:33?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 9:13-14 discusses the priestly role and inheritance in a spiritual context, echoing Joshua 13:33 where Levi’s inheritance is the LORD God Himself.

questions.question: What event or detail directly precedes the description of the Reubenite inheritance in Joshua 13:23?
options: The giving of the Ten Commandments
The crossing of the Jordan River
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:22 immediately precedes verse 23 and recounts the slaying of Balaam among the slain by Israel.

questions.question: In the cultural context of Joshua 13, why was the tribe of Levi given no land inheritance?
options: They were set apart as priests and received God as their inheritance
They refused to fight in battles
questions.correctAnswer: They were set apart as priests and received God as their inheritance
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:33 explains the Levites received no land because 'the LORD God of Israel was their inheritance,' reflecting their priestly and religious role.

questions.question: Which literary technique does Joshua 13:12 employ by referring to the 'remnant of the giants'?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:12 mentions the remnant of giants defeated by Moses, foreshadowing ongoing struggles with formidable enemies.

questions.question: How does Joshua 13:33 reflect a typological understanding of inheritance in biblical theology?
options: It presents God as the ultimate inheritance, prefiguring New Testament promises
It shows land as the only inheritance, emphasizing earthly possessions
It describes inheritance as only physical cities, excluding spiritual blessings
It limits inheritance to tribal boundaries, ignoring personal faith
questions.correctAnswer: It presents God as the ultimate inheritance, prefiguring New Testament promises
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:33 typologically portrays God as the Levites’ inheritance, anticipating the New Testament theme of believers’ spiritual inheritance in God.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 13:26, the border of the children of Gad included Ramathmizpeh and Betonim.
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:26 states, 'And from Heshbon unto Ramathmizpeh, and Betonim,' confirming these locations as part of Gad’s border.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Joshua 13:14 teach about the nature of God's provision for the Levites?
options: God provides a spiritual inheritance rather than a physical land inheritance
God excludes the Levites from any inheritance due to disobedience
The Levites receive a double portion of land as a special blessing
The Levites must conquer their own land by military means
questions.correctAnswer: God provides a spiritual inheritance rather than a physical land inheritance
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:14 states that 'Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the LORD God of Israel made by fire are their inheritance,' indicating a spiritual provision rather than a territorial one.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine judgment and human responsibility is taught in Joshua 13:6?
options: God will drive out the inhabitants from the land to fulfill His promise, requiring Israel's obedience
The inhabitants will remain permanently because of Israel's failure
God ignores the land's inhabitants and leaves the conquest to Israel alone
The inhabitants are allowed to coexist with Israel without any divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God will drive out the inhabitants from the land to fulfill His promise, requiring Israel's obedience
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:6 says 'All the inhabitants... them will I drive out from before the children of Israel,' affirming God's active judgment but also implying Israel must possess the land as commanded.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's faithfulness to His covenant promises is taught in Joshua 13:7?
options: God commands Joshua to divide the land to the tribes, fulfilling the promise to Abraham
God rescinds His promise and withholds the land from Israel
God leaves the land unassigned to test Israel's faith
God promises a new land outside Canaan to the tribes
questions.correctAnswer: God commands Joshua to divide the land to the tribes, fulfilling the promise to Abraham
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:7 directs Joshua to distribute the remaining land to the tribes, continuing the fulfillment of the covenant promise of land to Israel.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Joshua 13:1 specifically demonstrate in God's communication to Joshua?
questions.explanation: In Joshua 13:1, the LORD acknowledges Joshua's old age and reveals that much land remains to be possessed, showing God's complete knowledge of circumstances and future events.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by God's promise to drive out the inhabitants from Lebanon to Misrephothmaim in Joshua 13:6?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:6 shows God's sovereign authority over the land and peoples, declaring He will drive out inhabitants to give the land to Israel.

questions.question: How does Joshua 13:22's mention of Balaam connect to the broader biblical narrative of God's judgment on false prophecy?
options: It demonstrates God's judgment on those who misuse divine revelation for personal gain
It suggests Balaam was ultimately vindicated and blessed Israel
It implies God tolerates false prophets among His people
It shows Balaam's role as a faithful prophet to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God's judgment on those who misuse divine revelation for personal gain
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:22 states Balaam was slain among those defeated, underscoring divine judgment on false prophecy consistent with biblical warnings in Deuteronomy 18:20.

questions.question: In what way does Joshua 13:33's statement about the Levites' inheritance prepare for New Testament teachings on spiritual inheritance?
options: It anticipates the concept of believers receiving a spiritual inheritance rather than earthly possessions
It teaches that physical land is the ultimate inheritance for all believers
It denies any form of inheritance for God's people
It focuses exclusively on material blessings as the sign of God's favor
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the concept of believers receiving a spiritual inheritance rather than earthly possessions
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:33 emphasizes the LORD himself as the Levites' inheritance, foreshadowing New Testament themes of spiritual inheritance in Christ (e.g., Ephesians 1:11-14).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Joshua 13:14 and Joshua 13:33 teach about God's provision for the tribe of Levi?
options: God provides a non-territorial, spiritual inheritance as their true portion
God punishes Levi by withholding all blessings
Levi receives equal land inheritance as other tribes
Levi's inheritance is postponed until the Messiah comes
questions.correctAnswer: God provides a non-territorial, spiritual inheritance as their true portion
questions.explanation: Both verses 13:14 and 13:33 affirm that the Levites receive no land but instead the LORD Himself as inheritance, highlighting God's provision beyond material means.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about Israel's possession of the land is taught by Joshua 13:6 and Joshua 13:13?
options: God commands the expulsion of inhabitants but allows some to remain due to Israel's incomplete obedience
God permits all inhabitants to remain peacefully among Israel
Israel conquers the land solely through their own strength without divine aid
God abandons Israel in their conquest efforts
questions.correctAnswer: God commands the expulsion of inhabitants but allows some to remain due to Israel's incomplete obedience
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:6 states God will drive out inhabitants, but 13:13 notes that some tribes were not expelled, indicating human responsibility and failure in fully possessing the land.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine justice and mercy is taught by Joshua 13:22 and Joshua 13:13?
options: God executes judgment on enemies but shows mercy by allowing some groups to dwell with Israel
God shows no mercy and drives out all inhabitants without exception
God wholly ignores the sin of remaining inhabitants
God's justice is delayed and ineffective
questions.correctAnswer: God executes judgment on enemies but shows mercy by allowing some groups to dwell with Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:22 records the judgment on Balaam, while 13:13 notes some inhabitants remain, displaying a balance of justice and mercy in God's dealings.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Joshua 13:1-7 teaches that God abandoned Israel to possess the land alone. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God commands Joshua to divide the land and promises to drive out the inhabitants, showing divine involvement in Israel's conquest
God leaves Israel to conquer the land by their own power without any divine promise
God rescinds the land promise due to Israel's failure
God promises the land but forbids Israel from taking it
questions.correctAnswer: God commands Joshua to divide the land and promises to drive out the inhabitants, showing divine involvement in Israel's conquest
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:1-7 shows God actively directing the division of land and stating He will drive out inhabitants, affirming divine sovereignty and help rather than abandonment.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning God's covenant faithfulness and human agency is evident in Joshua 13:7 and Joshua 13:8?
options: God's covenant promises are fulfilled through His sovereign will and Israel's responsible obedience
God's promises are unconditional and independent of Israel's actions
Human agency alone determines possession of the land without God's role
God's promises are symbolic and not meant to be literally fulfilled
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant promises are fulfilled through His sovereign will and Israel's responsible obedience
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:7 commands division of the land and 13:8 references Moses' prior allocation, showing God's covenant faithfulness working through Israel's obedience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by God's instruction in Joshua 13:22 to slay Balaam the soothsayer?
questions.explanation: The execution of Balaam in Joshua 13:22 shows God's holiness and intolerance of false prophecy and sin among His people.

questions.question: How does the inheritance distribution described in Joshua 13:15-23 connect typologically to New Testament teachings on spiritual inheritance?
options: It prefigures the spiritual inheritance of believers as a fulfillment of God's promises beyond physical land
It teaches that only physical land inheritance matters for God's covenant
It denies any future inheritance to God's people
It restricts inheritance to exclusive tribal boundaries without spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the spiritual inheritance of believers as a fulfillment of God's promises beyond physical land
questions.explanation: The detailed land inheritance in Joshua anticipates the fuller spiritual inheritance described in the New Testament, where the promise extends beyond physical territory.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's justice and historical judgment is evident in Joshua 13:12 concerning the kingdom of Og and the 'remnant of the giants'?
options: God executes decisive judgment on sinful nations as part of His redemptive plan
God ignores the existence of giants and allows them to remain unchecked
God forgives all enemies without consequence
God's judgment is symbolic and not actual conquest
questions.correctAnswer: God executes decisive judgment on sinful nations as part of His redemptive plan
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:12 notes Moses smote and cast out the remnant of giants, indicating God's just judgment on enemies opposing His people.
